title: A Study on AI-Based Multimodal Authentication Methods to Prevent Deepfakes
content: Deepfakes refer to video, image, and audio data created using AI generation algorithms. With the rapid advancement of AI technology, anyone can now easily produce deepfake videos and images. If deepfake technology renders online and offline identity verification impossible, existing authentication systems—built through massive investment—will become obsolete. Therefore, research to address the risks associated with deepfake technology is urgently needed; this study proposes an AI-based multimodal authentication method to tackle this issue. The proposed method utilizes facial images as biometric features and spoken sentences as knowledge-based information. Additionally, it verifies users using olfactory characteristics, such as fruit scents. The model employed in this study features a feature-level multimodal authentication architecture. This architecture extracts information regarding faces, voices, and odors using CLS embeddings from pre-trained Transformers; it then aligns these data into a common 128-dimensional space and combines them using weighted integration to generate a unified user authentication feature. Experiments have demonstrated the feasibility of identity verification using these three modalities. Notably, the study proposes and validates the "Information-Balanced Adaptive Multimodal Weight Optimization (IB-AMWO)" algorithm, which enhances model performance by assigning balanced weights based on the information content of each modality. The IB-AMWO algorithm is expected to be effective in the field of anti-deepfake authentication, where it determines the authenticity of a user based on balanced information content, under the assumption that any modality could be forged.
